full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner arising out of an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure calls in question the judgment and decree dated 17-4-95 passed in Title Appeal No. 115 of 1991 by the Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Barisal reversing the judgment and decree dated 24-11-1990 passed in Title Suit No. 87 of 1988 by the Assistant Judge. Uzirpur Barisal decreeing the suit. 

 6. The trial Court on due consideration of the evidence and materials on record decreed the suit. 

 7. Although the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Barisal did not appear and contest the suit by filing vokalatnama and written statement, he alone challenged the aforesaid judgment and decree of the trial Court by filing Title Appeal No. 115 of 1991 in the Court of the District Judge, Barisal. Sub-sequently, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat. Barisal on transfer dismissing the suit by the judgment and decree dated 17-4-95. Hence, the plaintiff-petitioner filed the civil revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 8. Mr. M. Shamsul Alam, the learned Advocate appearing, for the plaintiff-petitioner, strenuously argues that since the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue), Barisal neither appeared through any lawyer by filing vokalatnama nor contested the suit by filing any written statement, he was not competent to file the appeal challenging the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Hence, the appellate Court below has committed gross illegality in entertaining and allowing the said appeal. The learned Advocate submits that since Ordinance No. 19 of 1959 does not empower the Government to forfeit any land for establishment of any Hat and Bazar, the impugned notification dated 6-1-76 forfeiting the suit land for establishment of a Hat was illegal and without jurisdiction. The learned Advocate next argues that since the SA recorded tenant of the suit land namely, Gopal Chandra Chottopadhya and the plaintiff-petitioner were and are all along in Bangladesh, the suit land was not liable to be treated as vested property and that too under VP Case No. 50/80, inasmuch as no order could be passed treating any property as enemy and vested property after the repeal of Ordinance No. 1 of 1969 on 23-3-1974. The appellate Court below erred in law in dismissing the suit by failing to appreciate this legal position obtaining in this case. 

 12. Although Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue). Barisal did not enter appearence and contest the suit, but he was nonetheless content to file the Appeal No. 115 of 1991 challenging the judgment and decree of the trial Court in view of section 96 and Order 41 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure Contention of Mr Alam that Addition Deputy Commissioner (Revenue). Barisal having failed to appear and contest the suit was incompetent to file the appeal has therefore no substance and is rejected. Even a third party, if he is aggrieved by the decree, can file an appeal. Case of H.M. Soya, & Co vs. Wazir Ali Industries Ltd 21 DLR (SC) 50 is an authority on the point. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-4-95 passed in Title Appeal No. 115 of 1991 by Me Shamsul Alam Khan, Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Barisal is set aside and the judgment and decree dated 24-11-90 passed by Mr Ranjan Kumar Saha, Assistant Judge, Wazirpur Barisal in Title Suit No. 87 of 1988 is hereby confirmed without any order as to cost.
